::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}

<!-- No caption here. This include is wrapped in a Quarto figure div in
     ch10-inversion-recovery.qmd, which supplies the caption so the figure
     is numbered and cross-referenceable like every other figure in the
     book. Adding a <p class="caption"> back would double it up. -->

<!-- Relies on figures.css, plotly-cartesian.min.js, qmrust_wasm.js (from
     includes/fig-t1-equations.qmd) and data-t1map.js + ir-shared.js (from
     includes/fig-ir-mag-vs-signal.qmd), all of which appear earlier in ch10. -->

<div class="qmrust-figure">

<p id="f-status" hidden style="font-size:12px;color:#a11;margin:0 0 10px"></p>

<div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:nowrap;gap:16px;align-items:flex-start;overflow-x:auto">
  <div id="f-curves" style="flex:1 1 430px;min-width:400px"></div>
  <div id="f-maps"   style="flex:0 0 250px"></div>
</div>

<!-- Keep every line here indented by at most three spaces. Markdown treats four
     leading spaces as an indented code block, which turns these controls into a
     <pre> of escaped tags instead of real inputs. -->
<div class="qmrust-controls">
 <div class="row">
  <label for="f-ti">TI = <b><span id="f-tival">0.60</span> s</b></label>
  <input id="f-ti" type="range" min="0" max="5" step="0.01" value="0.60">
 </div>
 <div class="row">
  <label for="f-te">TE = <b><span id="f-teval">8</span> ms</b></label>
  <input id="f-te" type="range" min="0" max="250" step="1" value="8">
 </div>
 <div class="row btns">
  <button id="f-null" type="button">Null CSF + T2-weight</button>
  <span id="f-readout"></span>
 </div>
</div>


</div>

<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var TNR = "Times New Roman";
  var CFGP = { showLink: false, displayModeBar: false, responsive: true };

  /* Signal model. With a 90 deg excitation the general inversion recovery
     equation loses its denominator (cos 90 = 0) and reduces to the grouped form
     the chapter derives, times the spin-echo factor:

         S = C exp(-TE/T2) (1 - 2 exp(-TI/T1) + exp(-(TR-TE)/T1))

     The recovery term uses TR - TE, not TR, to match eq-ch10-null-general in
     the chapter, which for a spin-echo readout writes it as TR - TE_last. This
     figure reads out a single echo, so the last echo is the only echo and
     TE_last = TE.

     qMRust evaluates the TI-dependent part (1 - 2 exp(-TI/T1)) through its
     inversion_recovery forward model with a = 1, b = -2. The exp(-(TR-TE)/T1)
     term and the exp(-TE/T2) scale are added per voxel afterwards. Keeping them
     out of the table is what lets TE stay instant: fold TE into the table and
     every TE step would mean rebuilding it with ~110 qMRust calls.

     T2 = T1/10 throughout, and lesion voxels get T1 x 1.1 and T2 x 2 -- the
     convention the qMRLab class example uses to build this phantom. */
  var T2_RATIO = 0.10, LES_T1 = 1.1, LES_T2 = 2.0;

  /* Two lesion sites, chosen offline as the most separated pair of solidly
     white-matter voxels lying 3-7 px from the ventricles in this map. Flat
     index is x*ny + y. */
  var LESIONS = [{ x: 41, y: 82, r: 2.6 }, { x: 78, y: 40, r: 2.6 }];

  /* TR is fixed. It is not a contrast control the reader is being asked to
     design here, and rebuilding the qMRust table on every change made it the
     one sluggish slider. 10 s is the usual T2-FLAIR value and the one the
     chapter quotes. */
  var TR = 10;
  var TE_T2W = 150;                 // TE the preset jumps to, in ms

  var TI_MAX = 5, NTI = 400;
  var NLUT = 260, NBIN = 110;
  var T1_LO = 0.05, T1_HI = 5.5;

  var TE_MAX = 0.25, NTE = 300;     // seconds, for the T2 decay panel

  var lutTi = IR.linspace(0.001, TI_MAX, NLUT);
  var tiGrid = IR.linspace(0.001, TI_MAX, NTI);
  var teGrid = IR.linspace(0.0, TE_MAX, NTE);
  var map = null, lesion = null, T2map = null;
  var lut = null;                       // TI-dependent table, built once
  var TISSUE = null;

  function buildPhantom() {
    map = IR.loadT1Map();
    var n = map.T1map.length, ny = map.ny;
    lesion = new Uint8Array(n);
    LESIONS.forEach(function (L) {
      for (var dx = -4; dx <= 4; dx++) {
        for (var dy = -4; dy <= 4; dy++) {
          if (dx * dx + dy * dy > L.r * L.r) { continue; }
          var x = L.x + dx, y = L.y + dy, v = x * ny + y;
          if (v < 0 || v >= n || !map.mask[v]) { continue; }
          var t = map.T1map[v];
          if (t > 0.70 && t < 1.15) { lesion[v] = 1; }   // only replace white matter
        }
      }
    });
    // Effective T1/T2 per voxel after the lesion substitution.
    T2map = new Float64Array(n);
    for (var v = 0; v < n; v++) {
      if (!map.mask[v] || !(map.T1map[v] > 0)) { continue; }
      var t1 = map.T1map[v], t2 = t1 * T2_RATIO;
      if (lesion[v]) { t1 *= LES_T1; t2 *= LES_T2 * LES_T1; }
      map.T1map[v] = t1;
      T2map[v] = t2;
    }
    var wm = 0.90, gm = 1.35, csf = 4.00;
    /* Colours are pinned per tissue rather than left to Plotly's colourway.
       The two panels are eight traces in one figure, so index-assigned colours
       would give the same tissue a different colour above and below. */
    TISSUE = [
      { label: "White matter", T1: wm,           T2: wm * T2_RATIO,                    c: "#1f77b4" },
      { label: "Grey matter",  T1: gm,           T2: gm * T2_RATIO,                    c: "#ff7f0e" },
      { label: "CSF",          T1: csf,          T2: csf * T2_RATIO,                   c: "#2ca02c" },
      { label: "Lesion",       T1: wm * LES_T1,  T2: wm * T2_RATIO * LES_T2 * LES_T1,  c: "#d62728" }
    ];
  }

  /** (1 - 2 e^-TI/T1) over a T1 x TI grid, via qMRust. TE-independent, so this
      is built once and both sliders read out of it. */
  function buildLut() {
    var cfg = IR.recipe(lutTi, "complex");
    var table = new Float64Array(NBIN * NLUT);
    for (var b = 0; b < NBIN; b++) {
      var T1 = T1_LO + (T1_HI - T1_LO) * (b + 0.5) / NBIN;
      table.set(IR.forward(cfg, T1, 1.0, -2.0), b * NLUT);
    }
    lut = table;
  }
  function bracket(T1, tiIdx, TE) {
    var b = Math.floor((T1 - T1_LO) / (T1_HI - T1_LO) * NBIN);
    return lut[Math.max(0, Math.min(NBIN - 1, b)) * NLUT + tiIdx] +
           Math.exp(-(TR - TE) / T1);
  }
  function tiIndex(ti) {
    var k = Math.round((ti - lutTi[0]) / (lutTi[1] - lutTi[0]));
    return Math.max(0, Math.min(NLUT - 1, k));
  }

  /** Nulling condition of the chapter: TI = T1 ln(2 / (1 + e^-TR/T1)). */
  function tiNull(T1, TR) { return T1 * Math.log(2 / (1 + Math.exp(-TR / T1))); }

  function state() {
    return { TR: TR,
             TI: parseFloat($("f-ti").value),
             TE: parseFloat($("f-te").value) / 1000 };
  }

  function image(s) {
    var k = tiIndex(s.TI), out = new Array(map.T1map.length);
    for (var v = 0; v < map.T1map.length; v++) {
      var t1 = map.T1map[v];
      if (!map.mask[v] || !Number.isFinite(t1) || t1 <= 0) { out[v] = null; continue; }
      out[v] = Math.abs(bracket(t1, k, s.TE) * Math.exp(-s.TE / T2map[v]));
    }
    return out;
  }

  /** Signal for one tissue at (TI, TE). */
  function sig(T1, T2, TI, TE, TRv) {
    return Math.abs((1 - 2 * Math.exp(-TI / T1) + Math.exp(-(TRv - TE) / T1)) *
                    Math.exp(-TE / T2));
  }

  /* Two stacked panels sharing one legend. The top is the inversion recovery the
     chapter has been drawing all along, signal against TI at the chosen TE. The
     bottom is the T2 decay that follows the excitation, signal against TE at the
     chosen TI -- the axis the reader has to move as well, and the one that
     actually separates lesion from white matter. Each panel carries a dotted
     line at the value the other panel is being evaluated at. */
  function drawCurves(s) {
    var traces = [];
    TISSUE.forEach(function (t, i) {
      var y = new Array(NTI);
      for (var k = 0; k < NTI; k++) { y[k] = sig(t.T1, t.T2, tiGrid[k], s.TE, s.TR); }
      traces.push({ x: tiGrid, y: y, mode: "lines", name: t.label, text: t.label,
                    hoverinfo: "x+y+text", legendgroup: t.label,
                    line: { color: t.c }, xaxis: "x", yaxis: "y" });
    });
    TISSUE.forEach(function (t) {
      var y = new Array(NTE);
      for (var k = 0; k < NTE; k++) { y[k] = sig(t.T1, t.T2, s.TI, teGrid[k], s.TR); }
      traces.push({ x: teGrid.map(function (v) { return v * 1000; }), y: y, mode: "lines",
                    name: t.label, text: t.label, hoverinfo: "x+y+text",
                    legendgroup: t.label, showlegend: false,
                    line: { color: t.c }, xaxis: "x2", yaxis: "y2" });
    });
    var nullCsf = tiNull(4.00, s.TR - s.TE);
    traces.push({ x: [nullCsf], y: [0], mode: "markers", name: "CSF null",
                  marker: { size: 11, color: "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
                            line: { color: "#333", width: 1.6 } },
                  xaxis: "x", yaxis: "y",
                  hovertemplate: "CSF null at TI = %{x:.2f} s<extra></extra>" });

    Plotly.react("f-curves", traces, {
      width: 430, height: 500, margin: { l: 58, r: 8, b: 48, t: 10 },
      xaxis:  IR.axis({ domain: [0, 1], anchor: "y",
                        title: { text: "Inversion Time – TI (s)",
                                 font: { family: TNR, size: 14 } } }),
      yaxis:  IR.axis({ domain: [0.58, 1], anchor: "x", range: [0, 1.05],
                        title: { text: "|S|", font: { family: TNR, size: 14 } } }),
      xaxis2: IR.axis({ domain: [0, 1], anchor: "y2",
                        title: { text: "Echo Time – TE (ms)",
                                 font: { family: TNR, size: 14 } } }),
      yaxis2: IR.axis({ domain: [0, 0.42], anchor: "x2", range: [0, 1.05],
                        title: { text: "|S|", font: { family: TNR, size: 14 } } }),
      legend: { x: 1, y: 1, xanchor: "right", yanchor: "top",
                font: { family: TNR, size: 11 }, bgcolor: "rgba(255,255,255,0.75)" },
      shapes: [
        { type: "line", x0: s.TI, x1: s.TI, xref: "x", yref: "y",
          y0: 0, y1: 1.05, line: { color: "#444", width: 1.5, dash: "dot" } },
        { type: "line", x0: s.TE * 1000, x1: s.TE * 1000, xref: "x2", yref: "y2",
          y0: 0, y1: 1.05, line: { color: "#444", width: 1.5, dash: "dot" } }
      ],
      plot_bgcolor: "white", paper_bgcolor: "white"
    }, CFGP);
  }

  function drawMap(s) {
    var blank = { showgrid: false, zeroline: false, showticklabels: false, ticks: "" };
    var z = image(s), hi = 0;
    for (var i = 0; i < z.length; i++) { if (z[i] > hi) { hi = z[i]; } }
    if (!(hi > 0)) { hi = 1; }
    Plotly.react("f-maps", [{
      type: "heatmap", z: IR.cropGrid(IR.grid(z, map.nx, map.ny, 0, 1), map.bbox),
      colorscale: [[0, "rgb(0,0,0)"], [1, "rgb(255,255,255)"]],
      zmin: 0, zmax: hi,
      colorbar: { title: { text: "|S|", side: "top", font: { family: TNR, size: 13 } },
                  thickness: 7, len: 0.72 },
      hovertemplate: "|S| = %{z:.3f}<extra></extra>"
    }], {
      width: 250, height: 330, margin: { t: 30, r: 2, b: 6, l: 2 },
      annotations: [{ text: "TI = " + s.TI.toFixed(2) + " s, TE = " +
                            Math.round(s.TE * 1000) + " ms",
                      x: 0.5, y: 1.10, xref: "paper", yref: "paper",
                      showarrow: false, font: { family: TNR, size: 15 } }],
      xaxis: Object.assign({ domain: [0, 0.88] }, blank),
      yaxis: Object.assign({ domain: [0, 1], scaleanchor: "x" }, blank),
      plot_bgcolor: "white", paper_bgcolor: "white"
    }, CFGP);
  }

  /* Lesion-to-white-matter separation, and how dark the fluid is -- the two
     numbers the class example asks the reader to trade off.

     The separation is expressed as a fraction of the brightest tissue in the
     image, not as (les-wm)/(les+wm). That normalised form is badly misleading
     here: at the opening TI of 0.60 s white matter is close to its own null, so
     white matter and lesion are 0.027 and 0.091 and the normalised contrast
     reads 56% -- while both are nearly black against CSF at 0.63, which is what
     sets the display window. Visibility depends on the difference relative to
     the range the image is actually stretched over, so that is what is
     reported. */
  function readout(s) {
    var q = function (t) { return sig(t.T1, t.T2, s.TI, s.TE, s.TR); };
    var wm = q(TISSUE[0]), les = q(TISSUE[3]), csf = q(TISSUE[2]), gm = q(TISSUE[1]);
    var span = Math.max(wm, les, csf, gm, 1e-6);
    $("f-readout").innerHTML =
      "lesion vs white matter <b>" + (100 * Math.abs(les - wm) / span).toFixed(0) +
      "%</b> of image range · CSF <b>" + csf.toFixed(3) + "</b>";
  }

  function redraw() {
    var s = state();
    $("f-tival").textContent = s.TI.toFixed(2);
    $("f-teval").textContent = Math.round(s.TE * 1000);
    drawCurves(s); drawMap(s); readout(s);
  }

  function fail(msg, e) {
    var el = $("f-status"); el.textContent = msg; el.hidden = false;
    if (e) { console.error(e); }
  }

  window.addEventListener("load", function () {
    if (typeof Plotly === "undefined") { fail("Plotly failed to load."); return; }
    wasm_bindgen({ module_or_path: "interactive/qmrust_wasm_bg.wasm" }).then(function () {
      setTimeout(function () {
        buildPhantom();
        buildLut();
        redraw();
        // Both are pure lookups against the precomputed table, so they can
        // track the drag.
        $("f-ti").addEventListener("input", redraw);
        $("f-te").addEventListener("input", redraw);
        // Both halves of the answer at once: TI on the CSF null, and a TE long
        // enough that the lesion actually separates from white matter.
        $("f-null").addEventListener("click", function () {
          $("f-te").value = String(TE_T2W);
          $("f-ti").value = tiNull(4.00, TR - TE_T2W / 1000).toFixed(2);
          redraw();
        });
      }, 20);
    }).catch(function (e) { fail("qMRust failed to start: " + e, e); });
  });
})();
</script>
